exposure: acquisition and persistence of vaginal Escherichia coli
Escherichia coli growth from cervical suture
cohort: The participants were 196 singleton pregnancies at high risk, who received an ultrasound-indicated or emergency cervical cerclage at the Royal Women's Hospital between 2004 and 2018.
finding: The acquisition and persistence of vaginal Escherichia coli, growth of Escherichia coli from the cervical suture, and acquisition of vaginal mixed anaerobes following cerclage insertion were significantly associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
